status: feature fix and real Session plus NativeWorld stepped cooldown regression pass against the terminal archives; normal gameplay/preview remains unverified
reported_behavior: In Celeste combat, an enemy that has attacked while in melee reach continues advancing toward the player until it attacks again.

visualEvidence.observations: Re-inspected the contiguous 375.250, 375.500, 375.750, 376.000 and 376.250 frames. They show a Warrior changing sword pose against the same visible Bog Moth; 375.500 and 376.000 show damage feedback while the moth remains near the combatants. At 377.250 the level-up tutorial is already on screen. The clip does not expose an NPC world transform, identify the reported Celeste encounter mob as this Bog Moth, or show a full attack-departure-to-next-attack interval, so it cannot directly prove post-melee cooldown displacement.
visualEvidence.classification: Direct frame inspection; insufficient evidence to infer NPC post-attack displacement. Use as temporal combat context only.

sourceFacts: monster_OnTargetInMeleeRange (lines 181-196) calls Stop before its SkillTree/RNG branch and Attack(GetTarget()); for actual Swamp_LizadMan_Type1 SkillTree resolves to -1, so source is Stop then Attack without a random draw.
monster_OnTargetOutOfRange (lines 108-116) calls MoveTo only when source AI state equals Idle and HasPath is false.

The existing generic controller retains ActorState.target_id as authority; while a tracked valid target is in melee range it calls request_actor_attack and does not invoke approach. Out-of-range transition invokes approach.

On initial target acquisition, current RuntimeEnemyController sets route based on melee distance but unconditionally invokes approach; an in-range newly acquired target can therefore retain moving state into the later attack request, bypassing the approach-to-attack Stop path. This is a concrete mismatch with the source melee event prefix.

The source `CSAttack::OnBlur` at 0x3c3f74 calls Character::GetAttackDelay at 0x3a3438 and starts timer42 with that millisecond value before pinning the body; the recovered Swamp lizard AI row supplies 800 ms. The delay begins at attack-state departure, not request time.

The recovered `monster_OnTargetInMeleeRange` in `port/android-native/app/src/main/assets/data/scripts/ai/monster.luac` lines 181-196 calls Stop before its SkillTree/RNG branch and Attack(GetTarget()); Swamp_LizadMan_Type1 resolves SkillTree to -1, so this actor takes Stop then Attack without a random draw. `monster_OnTargetOutOfRange` lines 108-116 calls MoveTo only when source state is Idle and HasPath is false.

NPC root-motion evidence in reports/npc-root-motion-source.json samples the genuine Swamp lizard Attack root groups at 0 XY travel for Attack0/Attack1/Attack2; Walk has authored XY travel. Thus any motion during an in-range cooldown should be investigated as stale Walk selection or body/solver drift, not suppressed attack root motion.
logicEvidence.coreLimits: The asset-backed same-Session regression observes an attack pose depart, permits the existing Session combo boundary to clear target_id for that completion sample, confirms next controller update reacquires the same target without an approach call, and tracks the authored 800 ms attack-delay interval. The focused cooldown extension binds the same lizard to NativeWorld and calls physical Stop from the same-actor controller stop service, then steps the world each 50 ms. Its body sleeps and stays stationary. It has no player body/contact pair, does not exercise an awake moving body, full source focus/pin composition or the normal product preview.

expectedBehavior: For a source monster admitted to melee, Stop the same existing navigation/controller actor before Attack or DoSkill. Preserve source-authored attack root motion; do not force idle during cooldown or broaden melee range. If the target truly leaves source melee reach, ordinary approach may resume under source range/state gates.

focusedTestPlan.sameSession: Feature test uses the actual Swamp_LizadMan_Type1 table/property/AI row and player in one CombatSession: acquire the in-range target; require stop before attack and no approach; begin the attack; then sample real 50 ms Session updates through animation departure, the 800 ms source attack delay, and the next attack. It records same ActorState position/action/target, pose ownership, request/approach/stop counts and actual resolved row delay.
focusedTestPlan.nativeWorld: The same focused test now binds the source lizard body to a real NativeWorld and calls PlayableActorBodies::step_world once before each active-controller Session update, matching recovered Level::Update physics-before-actor order. The controller Stop callback reaches stop_physical on that same ActorId/body. Each 50 ms sample logs native XY, sleeping flag, ActorState XYZ/action/target, attack-pose ownership and approach count. No player body/collision pair is added, so the test isolates this actor's post-Stop physical drift without inventing spacing or contact policy.
focusedTestPlan.cooldown: Private route-release runner compiles the actual asset-backed Session test against copied current terminal archives. The passing result observed the actual Swamp lizard Attack pose depart at frame 12 of the 50 ms sample loop, ActorState position remain (-6852.64, 938.285, 250), target remain canonical except the existing combo-clear completion sample then reacquire next controller update, no approach callback throughout, and next attack pose only after the source 800 ms departure cooldown.
focusedTestPlan.negativeBranches: A target outside the original melee kernel must enter shared approach; a target losing eligibility/death/view radius follows existing stop/cleanup. No guessed tolerance.
focusedTestPlan.outputs: Focused feature-owned test executable and JSONL body/ActorState trace under features/enemy_ai and .local-inputs; private output only, no shared archive or GUI.

uncertainties: Inspected v1.0.3 frames provide combat context but do not directly measure NPC position through cooldown.

The controller regression observed no ActorState position change and no approach callback during the actual same-Session lizard attack departure/cooldown/retry, but it did not include NativeWorld body integration.
Root motion evidence covers the recovered Swamp lizard Attack0/Attack1/Attack2 clips; another monster or attack variation can have authored root displacement.
A whole-product runtime/preview with the final integrated controller and body solver remains necessary to close the user-reported visual issue.

Missing reached stop fails closed. Existing tracked-target and approach-to-melee gates remain unchanged.
